title: What has this client liked before?
intro: These are your agency's own records for {client}: who was put forward, what the hiring managers did with them and what they said. It helps you find them again. It is not a score and not a recommendation.
loadError: Could not load the history. Try again.
fewHint: Based on fewer than {min} records. Read it as a hint, not as a pattern.
withheld: {count, plural, one {# value was left out because it names a protected characteristic.} other {# values were left out because they name a protected characteristic.}}

history.searchHint: A name, a position, an outcome or a reason
history.noCandidates: No candidate has been put forward to this client yet.
history.rounds: {count, plural, one {# interview round} other {# interview rounds}}
history.feedbackHint: Every rating given in interviews for this client, counted by criterion.
history.feedbackEmpty: No ratings have been recorded yet.
history.declineTitle: Why the hiring managers turned candidates down

patterns.intro: These describe what your records show. They do not say what will happen, and nothing here ranks or filters a person. Each row says how many records it comes from.
patterns.empty: There are no records to report on yet.
patterns.total: {records, plural, one {# candidate} other {# candidates}} in {positions, plural, one {# position} other {# positions}}.

interviewProfiles.title: Which candidate profiles lead to an interview?
interviewProfiles.measure: Of the candidates put forward, how many were invited to interview.

hireProfiles.title: Which candidate profiles lead to a hire?
hireProfiles.measure: Of the candidates put forward, how many were hired.

sources.title: Which sources bring quality candidates?
sources.measure: Quality here means the hiring manager wanted to interview the candidate: interviewed, of those put forward.

jdResponse.title: Which job descriptions get a high response?
jdResponse.measure: Of the candidates contacted, how many answered (yes or no).

dropOff.title: Where do candidates drop out?
dropOff.measure: Where candidates left the process without a hire, with the reason code when one was recorded.

hmPreferences.title: What do the hiring managers actually prefer?
hmPreferences.measure: Of the candidates the hiring manager decided on, how many were moved to an interview; and how they rated.

hireCharacteristics.title: Which job-related characteristics go with the people hired?
hireCharacteristics.measure: Only job-related things are used: level, years of experience, skills, source and how the reviewed match criteria were rated. Nothing about a person's age, gender, origin, family or the like is read or shown.

dropOff.total: {count, plural, one {# candidate left} other {# candidates left}} the process without a hire.

hm.decidedTitle: Moved to an interview, of those decided on

hire.hiresTitle: Among the {count, plural, one {# hire} other {# hires}}
hire.criteriaTitle: How the reviewed match analyses rated the criteria
hire.criteriaHint: Only analyses you marked as reviewed are counted. Strong on the criterion, among hires and among the others put forward.

summary.title: AI summary
summary.intro: On request, the assistant writes a short summary of these patterns. It sees counts only, never names, contact details or comments. Every sentence links to the records behind it. It stays a draft until you approve it.
summary.running: Reading the counts and writing the draft…
summary.none: No summary has been written yet.
summary.error: Could not write the summary. Try again.
summary.removed: {count, plural, =0 {Every sentence passed the check.} one {# sentence was removed because its numbers or wording did not check out.} other {# sentences were removed because their numbers or wording did not check out.}}
summary.empty: No sentences are left in this draft.
